meta.name: PhysAlts Multidisciplinary STEM & AI Timeline
meta.description: 44 fact-checked cross-disciplinary milestones from Euclid's Elements (c. 300 BCE) to test-time reasoning AI and autonomous science laboratories (2025–2026) spanning Mathematics, AI & CS, Biology & Genomics, Chemistry & Materials, Earth & Climate, and Engineering.

eras.label: Ancient & Classical Foundations
eras.summary: Axiomatic geometry, deductive proof, and early systematic natural history.

eras.label: Algebra, Algorithms & Printing
eras.summary: Systematic algebra, algorithmic arithmetic, and the movable-type printing revolution.

eras.label: Scientific Revolution & Enlightenment
eras.summary: Analytic geometry, cellular microscopy, quantitative chemistry, and immunization.

eras.label: Evolution, Elements & Early Computing
eras.summary: First computer algorithms, natural selection, Mendelian genetics, and the periodic law of elements.

eras.label: Information, Silicon & Molecular Life
eras.summary: Incompleteness, Turing machines, transistors, integrated circuits, DNA double helix, ARPANET, climate monitoring, and DNA sequencing.

eras.label: Genomes, Internet & Deep Learning
eras.summary: PCR, World Wide Web, Human Genome Project, CRISPR, Transformers, mRNA vaccines, AlphaFold, generative LLMs, and test-time reasoning AI.

events.title: Euclid's Elements & Axiomatic Geometry
events.summary: Compiled 13 books deriving plane and solid geometry plus elementary number theory (including the infinitude of primes) purely from five postulates and deductive logic.
events.impact: Established the axiomatic-deductive standard of mathematical proof that governed science for over two millennia.

events.title: Al-Khwarizmi's Al-Jabr & Algorithmic Arithmetic
events.summary: Authored 'The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing' (al-jabr), establishing algebra as an independent discipline, alongside treatises popularizing Hindu-Arabic decimal numerals.
events.impact: Gave the world the words 'algebra' (from al-jabr) and 'algorithm' (from his Latinized name Algorismi).

events.title: Gutenberg Movable-Type Printing Press
events.summary: Combined durable lead-tin-antimony alloy movable type, oil-based ink, and a mechanical screw press to mass-produce accurate books at a fraction of scribal cost.
events.impact: Enabled rapid, reproducible dissemination of scientific diagrams, mathematical tables, and experimental findings across Europe—igniting the Scientific Revolution.

events.title: Descartes' La Géométrie & Analytic Coordinate Systems
events.summary: Published La Géométrie as an appendix to Discourse on the Method, uniting Euclidean geometry with symbolic algebra by representing geometric curves as algebraic equations.
events.impact: Created Cartesian coordinates, making calculus, physics vector spaces, computer graphics, and machine-learning feature spaces possible.

events.title: Robert Hooke's Micrographia & Discovery of Biological Cells
events.summary: Published copperplate illustrations of the microscopic world using a compound microscope, coining the biological term 'cell' after observing the honeycomb compartments of cork.
events.impact: Launched cellular microscopy and opened the hidden microscopic universe later expanded by Antonie van Leeuwenhoek's discovery of bacteria.

events.title: Lavoisier's Conservation of Mass & Modern Chemistry
events.summary: Overthrew phlogiston theory in Traité Élémentaire de Chimie, demonstrating oxygen's role in combustion, defining chemical elements, and proving mass is strictly conserved in chemical reactions.
events.impact: Transformed chemistry from qualitative alchemy into a rigorous quantitative physical science.

events.title: Edward Jenner Pioneers Vaccination Against Smallpox
events.summary: Demonstrated experimentally that inoculation with mild cowpox (vaccinia) confers protective immunity against deadly smallpox.
events.impact: Founded modern immunology and led directly to the complete global eradication of smallpox in 1980, saving hundreds of millions of lives.

events.title: Ada Lovelace Publishes the First Computer Algorithm
events.summary: In Note G on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine, authored a step-by-step algorithm to compute Bernoulli numbers and envisioned general-purpose symbolic machines manipulating music and symbols beyond arithmetic.
events.impact: Articulated the conceptual leap from dedicated calculators to universal programmable software.

events.title: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species
events.summary: Presented overwhelming empirical evidence that all species descend with modification from common ancestors driven by natural selection.
events.impact: Unified all of biology under a single explanatory framework and inspired evolutionary algorithms in modern computer science.

events.title: Gregor Mendel's Laws of Discrete Genetic Inheritance
events.summary: Hybridized nearly 28,000 pea plants over eight years to prove heredity operates through discrete paired units ('factors', later called genes) obeying mathematical segregation ratios.
events.impact: Laid the quantitative foundation of classical genetics and the Modern Evolutionary Synthesis.

events.title: Dmitri Mendeleev's Periodic Table of the Elements
events.summary: Arranged chemical elements by atomic weight and recurring valence properties, boldly leaving gaps to predict the exact atomic weights and densities of undiscovered elements (gallium, scandium, germanium).
events.impact: Provided chemistry's master map and later revealed the quantum-mechanical shell structure of electrons.

events.title: Haber-Bosch Catalytic Ammonia Synthesis
events.summary: Converted inert atmospheric nitrogen (N2) and hydrogen under high pressure over metal catalysts into ammonia, scaled industrially at BASF by Carl Bosch.
events.impact: Enabled synthetic nitrogen fertilizers that today sustain nearly half of the global human population, while inspiring modern green electrocatalysis.

events.title: Alfred Wegener Proposes Continental Drift & Pangaea
events.summary: Synthesized matching coastlines, identical fossil species, and paleoclimate strata across oceans to argue continents slowly drift atop Earth's mantle.
events.impact: Foreshadowed the 1960s plate-tectonics revolution confirmed by seafloor spreading and mid-ocean ridge mapping.

events.title: Discovery & Development of Penicillin Antibiotics
events.figure: Alexander Fleming, Howard Florey & Ernst Chain
events.summary: Alexander Fleming noticed Penicillium mold lysing Staphylococcus bacteria at St Mary's Hospital, later purified into a life-saving drug by Florey, Chain, and Norman Heatley in Oxford.
events.impact: Ushered in the antibiotic era, transforming once-fatal bacterial infections and enabling modern surgery.

events.title: Kurt Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems
events.summary: Proved via Gödel numbering that any consistent formal axiomatic system capable of expressing elementary arithmetic contains true statements that cannot be proved within the system, nor can the system prove its own consistency.
events.impact: Shattered Hilbert's formalist dream of total mathematical completeness and directly inspired Turing's undecidability and computability theory.

events.title: Alan Turing Defines the Universal Computing Machine
events.summary: In 'On Computable Numbers', formalized the mathematical concept of an algorithm via an abstract tape machine (Turing machine) and proved the Halting Problem is uncomputable.
events.impact: Created theoretical computer science and proved a single stored-program universal machine can simulate any possible computation.

events.title: ENIAC: First Programmable Electronic General-Purpose Computer
events.figure: J. Presper Eckert, John Mauchly & ENIAC Programmers
events.summary: Completed at the University of Pennsylvania using nearly 18,000 vacuum tubes—programmed by six pioneering women mathematicians (Kay McNulty, Betty Jennings, Betty Snyder, Marlyn Wescoff, Fran Bilas, Ruth Lichterman)—computing thousands of times faster than electromechanical relays.
events.impact: Demonstrated high-speed electronic digital computing and directly catalyzed the von Neumann stored-program architecture.

events.title: Invention of the Semiconductor Transistor at Bell Labs
events.figure: John Bardeen, Walter Brattain & William Shockley
events.summary: Demonstrated the first solid-state point-contact germanium transistor amplifying electrical signals without fragile, power-hungry vacuum tubes.
events.impact: Became the fundamental atomic-scale switch of the Information Age—today exceeding 100 billion transistors per AI chip.

events.title: Claude Shannon Founds Information Theory
events.summary: Published 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication', defining the binary digit ('bit'), information entropy, lossless compression limits, and error-free channel capacity.
events.impact: Provided the mathematical blueprint for all digital telecommunications, Wi-Fi, 5G, data compression, and cross-entropy loss in neural networks.

events.title: Discovery of the DNA Double-Helix Structure
events.figure: Rosalind Franklin, Maurice Wilkins, James Watson & Francis Crick
events.summary: Combining Rosalind Franklin and Raymond Gosling's Photo 51 X-ray diffraction pattern at King's College London with structural model-building at Cambridge's Cavendish Lab revealed DNA's complementary double helix.
events.impact: Immediately explained the physical copying mechanism of heredity and launched the entire field of molecular biology.

events.title: Dartmouth Summer Research Project Coins 'Artificial Intelligence'
events.figure: John McCarthy, Marvin Minsky, Nathaniel Rochester & Claude Shannon
events.summary: Convened leading mathematicians and computer pioneers at Dartmouth College under the conjecture that 'every aspect of learning or any other feature of intelligence can in principle be so precisely described that a machine can be made to simulate it.'
events.impact: Formally launched Artificial Intelligence as a scientific discipline spanning symbolic reasoning, neural nets, and search.

events.title: The Keeling Curve Begins Continuous Atmospheric CO2 Tracking
events.summary: Installed precision infrared gas analyzers atop Mauna Loa (from Scripps Institution of Oceanography), recording both the biosphere's annual breathing cycle and the relentless rise of atmospheric CO2 from 315 ppm past 425 ppm.
events.impact: Became the foundational empirical record of modern climate science and anthropogenic greenhouse forcing.

events.title: Invention of the Monolithic Integrated Circuit (Microchip)
events.summary: Jack Kilby (Texas Instruments) built the first working germanium IC in 1958, while Robert Noyce (Fairchild Semiconductor) created the planar silicon integrated circuit in 1959 suited for mass photolithography.
events.impact: Unleashed Moore's Law—shrinking room-sized computers into smartphones, spacecraft guidance systems, and AI data centers.

events.title: First ARPANET Host-to-Host Packet-Switched Message
events.figure: Leonard Kleinrock, Charley Kline & Douglas Engelbart's Team
events.summary: On October 29, 1969, a UCLA computer transmitted the first packet-switched message ('LO' before crashing on 'LOGIN') to Stanford Research Institute over dedicated telephone lines.
events.impact: Established packet-switching infrastructure that evolved via TCP/IP (Cerf & Kahn) into the global Internet.

events.title: Invention of Low-Loss Silica Optical Fiber
events.figure: Robert Maurer, Donald Keck & Peter Schultz
events.summary: Following Charles Kao's theoretical prediction, Corning materials scientists fabricated fused-silica fiber with attenuation below 20 dB/km—making long-distance laser communication practical.
events.impact: Created the physical submarine and terrestrial photonic backbone carrying over 99% of transoceanic internet traffic.

events.title: Discovery of Deep-Sea Hydrothermal Vents & Chemosynthetic Life
events.figure: Robert Ballard, Jack Corliss & WHOI Alvin Team
events.summary: Diving 2,500 meters in WHOI's submersible Alvin, oceanographers discovered volcanic seafloor vents teeming with giant tube worms thriving without sunlight via chemosynthesis.
events.impact: Proved life can flourish solely on geothermal chemistry—redefining hypotheses on the origin of life and astrobiology on Europa and Enceladus.

events.title: Frederick Sanger Invents Chain-Termination DNA Sequencing
events.summary: Developed dideoxy chain-termination chemistry at MRC LMB to read exact nucleotide base sequences (A, C, G, T), earning Sanger his second Nobel Prize in Chemistry (1980).
events.impact: Provided the core reading engine of modern genomics and directly powered the first sequencing of the human genome.

events.title: Invention of Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)
events.summary: Conceived thermal-cycling exponential DNA amplification using heat-stable Taq polymerase, turning a single trace DNA molecule into billions of copies in hours.
events.impact: Indispensable cornerstone of medical diagnostics, ancient DNA paleogenomics, forensics, and genetic engineering.

events.title: Discovery of the Antarctic Ozone Hole & Montreal Protocol
events.figure: Joe Farman, Brian Gardiner & Jonathan Shanklin (BAS)
events.summary: British Antarctic Survey atmospheric scientists published decades of Dobson spectrophotometer measurements revealing catastrophic springtime stratospheric ozone depletion caused by human-made CFCs.
events.impact: Triggered the 1987 Montreal Protocol—the most successful international environmental treaty in history—setting the ozone layer on track to recover.

events.title: Backpropagation Popularized for Multi-Layer Neural Networks
events.figure: David Rumelhart, Geoffrey Hinton & Ronald Williams
events.summary: Demonstrated in Nature that reverse-mode automatic differentiation (backpropagation) efficiently learns internal hidden representations inside multi-layer neural networks.
events.impact: Became the universal optimization engine training virtually every modern deep learning and foundation AI model.

events.title: Tim Berners-Lee Invents the World Wide Web at CERN
events.summary: Invented HTTP, HTML, and URLs at CERN so particle physicists across global universities could seamlessly share hyperlinked documents—then released the protocol into the public domain royalty-free in 1993.
events.impact: Transformed global knowledge sharing, commerce, open science, and provided the training substrate for modern AI.

events.title: Andrew Wiles Proves Fermat's Last Theorem
events.summary: Solved Pierre de Fermat's 358-year-old conjecture by proving the Modularity Theorem for semistable elliptic curves, uniting algebraic number theory and modular forms.
events.impact: Advanced the Langlands Program and earned Andrew Wiles the 2016 Abel Prize.

events.title: Completion of the Human Genome Project
events.summary: An international public consortium across 20 centers in six countries mapped and released ~3 billion base pairs of human euchromatic DNA freely online under the Bermuda Principles.
events.impact: Catalyzed genomic medicine, plummeting sequencing costs by more than a million-fold and launching precision oncology and population genomics.

events.title: Grigori Perelman Proves the Poincaré & Geometrization Conjectures
events.summary: Posted three landmark preprints on arXiv mastering Richard Hamilton's Ricci flow with surgery to classify all compact 3-manifolds and resolve Henri Poincaré's 1904 topology conjecture.
events.impact: Solved the first (and thus far only) Clay Millennium Prize Problem, demonstrating the power of open arXiv dissemination.

events.title: Shinya Yamanaka Discovers Induced Pluripotent Stem (iPS) Cells
events.summary: Demonstrated that introducing just four transcription factors (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) reprograms mature adult skin cells back into embryonic-like pluripotent stem cells.
events.impact: Revolutionized regenerative medicine, personalized disease modeling, and 3D human organoids (2012 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine).

events.title: AlexNet Ignites the GPU Deep Learning Revolution
events.figure: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever & Geoffrey Hinton
events.summary: Trained a deep convolutional neural network on two consumer NVIDIA GPUs using ReLU activations and dropout, slashing ImageNet classification error by over 10 percentage points.
events.impact: Proved GPU-accelerated deep neural networks outperform hand-engineered features, triggering the modern AI explosion.

events.title: CRISPR-Cas9 Programmable RNA-Guided Genome Editing
events.figure: Jennifer Doudna, Emmanuelle Charpentier, Martin Jinek & Krzysztof Chylinski
events.summary: Repurposed a bacterial immune defense into a programmable molecular scissor using a single guide RNA (sgRNA) to cut any chosen DNA sequence with pinpoint precision.
events.impact: Democratized gene editing worldwide, won the 2020 Chemistry Nobel, and led to the first FDA/MHRA-approved CRISPR sickle-cell therapy (2023).

events.title: DeepMind's AlphaGo Defeats Go World Champion Lee Sedol
events.figure: David Silver, Demis Hassabis & Google DeepMind Team
events.summary: Combined deep policy/value neural networks with Monte Carlo Tree Search and self-play reinforcement learning to defeat 18-time world champion Lee Sedol 4–1—playing the iconic creative 'Move 37'.
events.impact: Demonstrated superhuman intuitive strategic reasoning a decade ahead of expectations and established the search + RL paradigm behind modern reasoning AI.

events.title: 'Attention Is All You Need': Invention of the Transformer
events.figure: Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, Jakob Uszkoreit, Llion Jones, Aidan Gomez, Łukasz Kaiser & Illia Polosukhin
events.summary: Replaced sequential recurrent networks with parallelizable multi-head self-attention layers, enabling massive scaling across thousands of GPUs/TPUs on internet-scale sequences.
events.impact: Became the universal neural backbone of modern LLMs (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, DeepSeek), multimodal vision, protein models, and DNA foundation models.

events.title: Nucleoside-Modified mRNA Vaccines Validated Globally
events.figure: Katalin Karikó, Drew Weissman & Global mRNA Teams
events.summary: Decades of foundational RNA modification work (pseudouridine substitution preventing destructive inflammation, paired with lipid nanoparticles) enabled safe, >90%-effective COVID-19 vaccines designed within days of viral sequencing.
events.impact: Saved millions of lives, earned the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, and opened a programmable platform for personalized cancer vaccines.

events.title: AlphaFold 2 Solves the 50-Year Protein Folding Challenge
events.figure: John Jumper, Demis Hassabis & Google DeepMind
events.summary: Achieved atomic-level accuracy predicting 3D protein structures directly from 1D amino-acid sequences at CASP14, then openly released 200M+ predicted structures with EMBL-EBI.
events.impact: Transformed structural biology overnight and ushered in the AI-for-Science era, winning the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

events.title: ChatGPT & General-Purpose Large Language Models Go Global
events.summary: Combined large-scale generative pre-training with instruction tuning and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), reaching 100 million users in two months.
events.impact: Catalyzed worldwide deployment of conversational AI assistants, code generation, multimodal reasoning, and open-weight model ecosystems.

events.title: AlphaFold 3, De Novo Protein Design & the AI Science Nobels
events.figure: Demis Hassabis, John Jumper, David Baker, Geoffrey Hinton & John Hopfield
events.summary: AlphaFold 3 extended atomic diffusion prediction to proteins, DNA, RNA, and small-molecule drugs, while both the 2024 Physics and Chemistry Nobel Prizes recognized foundational neural networks and AI protein science.
events.impact: Cemented artificial intelligence as a core foundational instrument of physics, chemistry, and molecular biology.

events.title: Test-Time Reasoning AI, Open Reasoning Models & Autonomous Science Labs
events.figure: Global AI & Scientific Computing Community (OpenAI, DeepMind, Anthropic, DeepSeek, Arc, LBNL)
events.summary: Reinforcement learning on verifiable math, coding, and science problems unlocked inference-time scaling (o-series, DeepSeek-R1, Claude/Gemini reasoning), formal theorem proving (Lean 4), genomic foundation models (Evo 2), and robotic closed-loop wet labs.
events.impact: Marks the transition from passive pattern-matching models to active scientific reasoning agents collaborating directly with mathematicians, physicists, and biologists.
